claims.claim: The reference managers span private equity, credit, real assets and/or perpetual or insurance-linked capital rather than a single buyout strategy.

The reference materials describe a recurring bundle of institutional structures and capabilities: control rights, operating resources, proprietary sourcing, capital-structure flexibility and long-duration capital. This is an analytical map, not causal return attribution.
claims.classification: cross-source analytical synthesis; not performance attribution

claims.claim: Cash-flow resilience, debt-service/refinancing capacity and collateral/asset quality are the useful public-market analogue of a credit-first underwriting lens.
Operating improvement can be credited only when a public company has disclosed measurable actions and the analyst can monitor the KPI; a retail investor cannot compel the action.
Ordinary China secondary-market exit planning must not assume an intraday sale; purchased securities may not be sold before settlement unless an instrument-specific reverse-trading exception applies.
claims.classification: current exchange-rule boundary; S09 operative DOCX and deferred-provisions attachment locally archived

claims.claim: Margin financing and securities lending are not an appropriate substitute for a retail LBO; the framework defaults to no borrowing and no naked short exposure.
claims.classification: current exchange-rule context plus conservative framework choice

claims.claim: Publicly offered real-estate REITs are only a partial analogue to real-asset cash-flow investing. Each project requires operating, leverage, valuation, governance and liquidity work; its applicable underlying-asset rules and product documents must be checked separately.
claims.classification: documented rule context plus analytical translation

claims.claim: ETF creation/redemption and reverse-trading mechanics are category- and rule-specific: S09 enumerates specified same-day reverse-trading categories, while a category-specific ETF mechanism does not remove the need to model secondary-market exit constraints for a given ETF strategy.
claims.classification: current exchange rule plus framework application; S09 operative DOCX locally archived

claims.claim: No source package here supports a named security, product suitability conclusion, expected-return forecast or live allocation.
